Thus will the Lord execute judgments upon Moab. <reference osisRef="Ezek.25.11">Eze 25:11</reference> sums up what is affirmed concerning Moab in <reference osisRef="Ezek.25.9">Eze 25:9</reference> and <reference osisRef="Ezek.25.10">Eze 25:10</reference>, in the one idea of the judgments of God upon this people. <div eID="gen15025" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen15026" type="x-p"/> The execution of these judgments commenced with the subjugation of the Ammonites and Moabites by Nebuchadnezzar, five years after the destruction of Jerusalem (vid., Josephus, <hi type="italic">Antt</hi>. x. 9. 7, and M. von Niebuhr, <hi type="italic">Gesch. Assurs,</hi> etc., p. 215). Nevertheless the Ammonites continued to exist as a nation for a long time after the captivity, so that Judas the Maccabaean waged war against them (1 Macc. 5:6, 30-43); and even Justin Martyr speaks of  ̓Αμμανιτῶν νῦν πολὺ πληθος (<hi type="italic">Dial. Tryph</hi>. p. 272). - But Origen includes their land in the general name of Arabia (lib. i. <hi type="italic">in Job</hi>). The name of the Moabites appears to have become extinct at a much earlier period. After the captivity, it is only in Ezr 9:1; <reference osisRef="Neh.13.1">Neh 13:1</reference>, and <reference osisRef="Dan.11.41">Dan 11:41</reference>, that we find any notice of them as a people. Their land is mentioned by Josephus in the <hi type="italic">Antiq</hi>. xiii. 14. 2, and xv. 4, and in the <hi type="italic">Bell. Jud</hi>. iii. 3. 3. - A further fulfilment by the Messianic judgment, which is referred to in Zep 2:10, is not indicated in these words of Ezekiel; but judging from the prophecy concerning the Edomites (see the comm. on <reference osisRef="Ezek.25.14">Eze 25:14</reference>), it is not to be excluded.
entries.557d390d02825c75a6e68e09a3d97befbade7416: <reference osisRef="Ezek.25.12-Ezek.25.14">Eze 25:12-14</reference> <div eID="gen15026" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s2">Against the Edomites</title> <div sID="gen15027" type="x-p"/> Eze 25:12. <hi type="italic">Thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Because Edom acteth revengefully towards the house of Judah, and hath been very guilty in avenging itself upon them,</hi> Eze 25:13. <hi type="italic">Therefore, thus saith the Lord Jehovah, I will stretch out my hand over Edom, and cut off man and beast from it, and make it a desert from Teman, and unto Dedan they shall fall by the sword.</hi> Eze 25:14. <hi type="italic">And I will inflict my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel, that they may do to Edom according to my anger and my wrath; and they shall experience my vengeance, is the saying of the Lord Jehovah</hi>. - Whilst the Ammonites and the Moabites are charged with nothing more than malicious pleasure at the fall of Israel, and disregard of its divine calling, the Edomites are reproached with revengeful acts of hostility towards the house of Judah, and threatened with extermination in consequence. The עשׂות, doing or acting of Edom, is more precisely defined as 'בּנקום וגו, i.e., as consisting in the taking of vengeance, and designated as very guilty, ישׁמוּ אשׁום. עשׂה, followed by בּ with an infinitive, as in Eze 17:17. Edom had sought every opportunity of acting thus revengefully towards Israel (vid., Oba 1:11; <reference osisRef="Amos.1.11">Amo 1:11</reference>), so that in <reference osisRef="Ezek.35.5">Eze 35:5</reference> Ezekiel speaks of the “eternal enmity” of Edom against Israel. For this reason we must not restrict the reproach in <reference osisRef="Ezek.25.12">Eze 25:12</reference> to particular outbreaks of this revenge at the time of the devastation and destruction of Judah by the Chaldeans, of which the Psalmist complains in <reference osisRef="Ps.137.1-Ps.137.9">Psa 137:1-9</reference>, and for which he invokes the vengeance of God upon Edom. Man and beast are to be cut off from Edom in consequence, and the land to become a desert from Teman to Dedan. These names denote not cities, but districts. <hi type="italic">Teman</hi> is the southern portion of Idumaea (see the comm. on <reference osisRef="Amos.1.12">Amo 1:12</reference>); and <hi type="italic">Dedan</hi> is therefore the northern district. <hi type="italic">Dedan</hi> is probably not the Cushite tribe mentioned in <reference osisRef="Gen.10.7">Gen 10:7</reference>, but the tribe of the same name which sprang from the sons of Abraham by Keturah (<reference osisRef="Gen.25.3">Gen 25:3</reference>), and which is also mentioned in <reference osisRef="Jer.49.8">Jer 49:8</reference> in connection with Edom. דּדנה has ה local with <hi type="italic">Seghol</hi> instead of <hi type="italic">Kametz</hi>, probably on account of the preceding <hi type="italic">a</hi> (vid., Ewald, §216 <hi type="italic">c</hi>). There is no necessity to connect מתּימן with the following clause, as Hitzig and Kliefoth have done, in opposition to the accents. The two geographical names, which are used as a periphrasis for Idumaea as a whole, are distributed equally through the <hi type="italic">parallelismus membrorum</hi> between the two clauses of the sentence, so that they belong to both clauses, so far as the sense is concerned. Edom is to become a desert from Teman to Dedan, and its inhabitants from Teman to Dedan are to fall by the sword. This judgment of vengeance will be executed by God through His people Israel. The fulfilment of this threat, no doubt, commenced with the subjugation of the Edomites by the Maccabees; but it is not to be limited to that event, as Rosenmüller, Kliefoth, and others suppose, although the foundation was thereby laid for the disappearance of the national existence of Edom. For it is impossible with this limitation to do justice to the emphatic expression, “<hi type="italic">my people</hi> Israel.” On the ground, therefore, of the prophecies in <reference osisRef="Amos.9.12">Amo 9:12</reference> and Oba 1:17, that the people of God are to take possession of Edom, when the fallen tabernacle of David is raised up again, i.e., in the Messianic times, which prophecies point back to that of Balaam in Num 24:18, and have their roots, as this also has, in the promise of God concerning the twin sons of Isaac, “the elder shall serve the younger” (<reference osisRef="Gen.25.23">Gen 25:23</reference>), we must seek for the complete fulfilment in the victories of the people of God over all their foes, among whom Edom from time immemorial had taken the leading place, at the time when the kingdom of God is perfected. For even here Edom is not introduced merely as a single nation that was peculiarly hostile to Judah, but also as a type of the implacable enmity of the heathen world towards the people and kingdom of God, as in <reference osisRef="Ezek.35.1-Ezek.35.15">Eze 35:1-15</reference>, Isa. 34:63, etc. The vengeance, answering to the anger and wrath of Jehovah, which Israel, as the people of God, is to execute upon Edom, consists not merely in the annihilation of the national existence of Edom, which John Hyrcanus carried into effect by compelling the subjugated Edomites to adopt circumcision (see the comm. on Num 24:18), but chiefly in the wrathful judgment which Israel will execute in the person of Christ upon the arch-enemy of the kingdom of God by its complete extinction.
entries.5ff945e813b7ae28a7291468177fadaa0499a47c: <reference osisRef="Ezek.25.15-Ezek.25.17">Eze 25:15-17</reference> <div eID="gen15027" type="x-p"/> <title type="x-s2">Against the Philistines</title> <div sID="gen15028" type="x-p"/> Eze 25:15. <hi type="italic">Thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Because the Philistines act with revenge, and avenge themselves with contempt in the soul to destroy in everlasting enmity,</hi> Eze 25:16. <hi type="italic">Therefore thus saith the Lord Jehovah, Behold, I will stretch out my hand over the Philistines, and cut off the Cretans, and destroy the remnant by the seashore.</hi> Eze 25:17. <hi type="italic">And I will execute great vengeance upon them through chastisements of wrath, and they shall know that I am Jehovah, when I bring my vengeance upon them.</hi> - The Philistines resembled the Edomites and Ammonites in their disposition towards the covenant nation, the former in their thirst for revenge, the latter in their malicious rejoicing at Israel’s fall. For this reason they had already been classed by Isaiah (<reference osisRef="Isa.11.14">Isa 11:14</reference>) with Edom, Moab, and Ammon as enemies, who would be successfully attacked and overcome by Israel, when the Lord had gathered it again from its dispersion. In the description of its sin towards Israel we have a combination of elements taken from the conduct of Edom and Ammon (vv. 12 and 6). They execute revenge with contempt in the soul (שׁאט בּנפשׁ, as in v. 6), with the intention to destroy (למשׁחית) Israel; and this revenge springs from eternal, never-ending hostility. The Lord will cut off the whole of the people of the Philistines for this. כּרתים, Cretans, originally a branch of the Philistian people, settled in the south-west of Canaan. The name is used by Ezekiel for the people, as it had already been by Zephaniah (Zep 2:5), for the sake of the <hi type="italic">paronomasia</hi> with הכרתּי. The origin of the name is involved in obscurity, as the current derivation from <hi type="italic">Creta</hi> rests upon a very doubtful combination (cf. Stark, <hi type="italic">Gaza</hi>, pp. 66 and 99ff.). By the “remnant of the sea-coast,” i.e., the remnant of the inhabitants of the coast of the Mediterranean, in other words, of the Philistines, the destruction of which had already been predicted by Amos (<reference osisRef="Amos.1.8">Amo 1:8</reference>), Isaiah (<reference osisRef="Isa.14.30">Isa 14:30</reference>), and Jeremiah (<reference osisRef="Jer.42.4">Jer 42:4</reference>), we are to understand the whole nation to the very last man, all that was still left of the Philistines (see the comm. on <reference osisRef="Amos.1.8">Amo 1:8</reference>). - The execution of the vengeance threatened by God began in the Chaldean period, in which Gaza was attacked by Pharaoh, and, judging from <reference osisRef="Jer.47.1-Jer.47.7">Jer 47:1-7</reference>, the whole of Philistia was laid waste by the Chaldeans (see the fuller comments on this in the exposition of <reference osisRef="Jer.47.1-Jer.47.7">Jer 47:1-7</reference>). But the ultimate fulfilment will take place in the case of Philistia also, through the Messianic judgment, in the manner described in the commentary on Zep 2:10.  <chapter eID="Ezek.25"/> <div eID="gen15028" type="x-p"/>
